A 70-year-old woman visited the outpatient breast clinic due to changes in the skin of her left breast. She observed skin discoloration 6 months prior, which progressively increased, prompting her to seek medical attention. Her medical history includes hypertension, hyperlipidemia, diabetes mellitus, and osteoporosis, with no previous breast health issues or surgeries. She reported no associated symptoms such as pain, new masses, nipple discharge/retraction, or lymphadenopathy. During the physical examination, her vital signs were within normal limits, and she appeared to be in no distress. The breast examination revealed a single 3 × 3 cm pink, non-tender, raised lesion on the left breast at the 12:00 position. The patient agreed to a treatment procedure and tolerated it well without any complications.
